chain.g: first degree or note of Guido of Arezzo's hexachordal scales

ety.text: From Middle English ut (“first degree or note of Guido of Arezzo's hexachordal scales”), Italian ut in the solmization of Guido of Arezzo, from the opening word Latin ut (“how”) in the lyrics of the scale-ascending hymn Ut queant laxis by Benedictine monk Paulus Deacon (8th c. CE).

senses.d: Syllable (formerly) used in solfège to represent the first note of a major scale.
ex: Old Mantuam, old Mantuan. Who vnderſtandeth thee not, vt re ſol la mi fa: Vnder pardon sir, What are the contents? […]

grp.label: first note of a major scale
